page: Amazon Web Services m6a.32xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 128 virtual CPUs mapped to 64 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.6 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing hyperthreading with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is 512.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU tests placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is also in the top 10%, while large-block read and write speeds remain strong in the top 25%. In database operations, the instance achieves top-tier performance, processing 129.17 million Redis SET operations per second. Software compilation and image processing benchmarks register as strong, while single-threaded tasks, such as gzip compression and Geekbench single-core tests, perform in the average range.

Due to the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs, workloads requiring high-speed local disk caching or hardware-accelerated machine learning training are not suitable without external network-attached storage. However, the high virtual core count and substantial memory bandwidth make it highly efficient for memory-intensive general-purpose workloads. It is well-suited for large-scale database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and multi-threaded enterprise applications.
description: Amazon Web Services m6a.32xlarge is a general-purpose server instance featuring 128 vCPUs and 512.0 GB of DDR4 RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.6 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it delivers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs but provides a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth, alongside strong database processing capabilities, such as 129.17 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-threaded performance and text processing fall into the average range. This hardware profile is optimized for multi-threaded enterprise applications, large-scale database operations, software compilation, and static web serving.
